justification: Changes whether the capacity card is shown for community-title (classsubtype=4) lots — a user-facing output change in a liability-sensitive area, so critical tier. The change is narrow and conservative: it feeds the authoritative cadastre classsubtype community signal that classify_strata already routes to DEVELOPMENT; classsubtype=3 strata is unchanged, so no stacked apartment can be promoted to a development brief.

pre_impl.existing_data: get_cadastral_info already fetches classsubtype and hasstratum from the NSW cadastre; classify_strata already routes plan_type in (community, neighbourhood) to DEVELOPMENT, locked by test_strata_classify_lotcount.py::test_community_title_beats_lot_count. The brief switch (intelligence_brief.py) sends APARTMENT and AMBIGUOUS to a RenovationBrief with no capacity card.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The code assumed a community lot always carries a CP planlabel prefix. Live data (25 Empire St Haberfield: classsubtype=4, planlabel DP1252132) shows community-title lots can carry a DP-style prefix, so the prefix-only rule mislabelled them strata and the brief hid the capacity card.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new file, query, or table. One boolean derives plan_type from classsubtype==4 OR the existing CP prefix. classsubtype=3 behaviour is unchanged; only classsubtype=4 lots flip from strata to community, which downstream routing already handles.
pre_impl.external_source_error: If the cadastre query raises or returns no features, get_cadastral_info returns its existing default non-strata dict; the new branch is reached only when sp_lots is non-empty, so a source failure cannot trigger a wrong community classification or a wrongly-shown card.
pre_impl.frontend_type: Backend only. The cadastre dict shape is unchanged (same keys and types); only the plan_type string value changes for classsubtype=4 lots, which classify_strata already consumes. No frontend interface change.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: a community-title developable lot was classed AMBIGUOUS and shown a RenovationBrief with no capacity card (a silent under-serve). After: it routes to DEVELOPMENT and shows the indicative, subject-to-a-DA capacity range like any house, while a genuine apartment (classsubtype=3) is unaffected and still gets the renovation brief.

functions.name: get_cadastral_info
functions.input: the latitude and longitude of the subject property, used to query the NSW cadastre lot layer
functions.output: a cadastre dict whose plan_type now reflects the classsubtype community-title code, not just the planlabel prefix
functions.if_none: on a query exception or an empty feature list it returns the existing default non-strata dict unchanged, exactly as before

values: N/A - no regulatory values are hardcoded or changed. classsubtype=4 is the NSW cadastre community-title code and plan_type is an internal classification label, not a planning value.
queries: N/A - this change adds no new database or API query; it only reinterprets the classsubtype field already returned by the existing NSW cadastre query inside get_cadastral_info.

break_it.scenario: A genuine stacked strata apartment lot (classsubtype 3) must not be promoted to community or development by this change
break_it.what_happens: if classsubtype 3 leaked into the community branch a real apartment would wrongly be shown a development capacity card
break_it.how: the community branch triggers only when classsubtype equals 4 or the planlabel starts with CP, so classsubtype 3 stays strata and routes unchanged

break_it.scenario: A community-title lot carrying a DP-style planlabel was mislabelled strata and hidden in the AMBIGUOUS band
break_it.what_happens: the developable lot was shown a renovation brief with an empty capacity card, a silent and confusing under-serve
break_it.how: plan_type is now derived from the authoritative classsubtype community code, so the lot routes to DEVELOPMENT and the capacity card is shown

break_it.scenario: The cadastre query itself fails or returns no features for the supplied coordinate
break_it.what_happens: a naive change could crash the function or emit a wrong default classification for the subject lot
break_it.repro: code review of get_cadastral_info: the except branch and the empty attrs_list branch both return the unchanged default non-strata dict
break_it.how: the new is_community boolean lives inside the existing if sp_lots branch, so an error or empty result never reaches it

break_it.scenario: The downstream StrataHub lot-count query is unavailable so no unit count is present for the lot
break_it.what_happens: classification could fall back to the weak area heuristic and route a genuine strata lot to the wrong state
break_it.how: the plan_type community signal is checked before the lot count, so a community lot still routes to DEVELOPMENT and a classsubtype 3 lot without a count stays AMBIGUOUS rather than being shown a card

post_merge.manual_verify: Run a live brief on 25 Empire St Haberfield — it should now return a development brief with the indicative capacity range rather than a renovation brief. Confirm a known apartment address (classsubtype 3, e.g. 10 Orpington St Ashfield) still returns the renovation brief with no capacity card. The 20m cadastre buffer taint and the StrataHub coverage gap remain open follow-ups (see ce-bug4-strata-capacity-salvage-2026-06.md).
